newsitem.title: CHINA: Flight leaves Beijing in sign Korea defector gone.
newsitem.headline: Flight leaves Beijing in sign Korea defector gone.

text.p: A special flight left Beijing on Tuesday amid reports North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop had been spirited out of the South Korean mission in the Chinese capital where he had been sheltering for nearly five weeks.

The flight took off from a military airport on the outskirts of Beijing at 7 a.m. (2300 GMT) and arrived about 2-1/2 hours later in the southeastern coastal city of Xiamen, aviation officials in Xiamen said.
The aircraft was carrying a passenger who would take a scheduled flight to Manila at about 10.10 a.m. (0210 GMT), one official said by telephone.
In Seoul, the Yonhap Television News quoted a South Korean government source as saying Hwang, the most senior leader to flee Stalinist North Korea, had left Beijing.
Japan's Fuji Television said Hwang slipped out of Seoul's heavily guarded Beijing mission in an unmarked vehicle on Monday evening.
Pyongyang's top ideological theoretician spent the night at the military airport on the outskirts of Beijing before being flown out of the Chinese capital, the station said.
Xiamen airport officials said they were unable to identify the passenger aboard the special aircraft from Beijing but said he was scheduled to take a Southern Airlines flight to Manila.
The passenger's route matched the one Hwang was expected to take when he ended weeks of diplomatic limbo at the centre of a diplomatic crisis between Beijing and the two rival Koreas.
Security remained tight on Tuesday morning around the South Korean consulate in Beijing where Hwang sought shelter on February 12.
A South Korean Foreign Ministry spokesman declined to comment on the report that Hwang had left Beijing, saying Beijing and Seoul would announce his departure after he left.
South Korea's influential Chosun Ilbo newspaper said Hwang and an aide who sought asylum with him slipped out of South Korea's consulate overnight.
On Monday a senior South Korean official said Hwang would stay in a third country "for a considerable period of time" before coming to South Korea.
